assumptions: a label adverse effect on the same clinical axis as a patient phenotype is a potential collision; a pharmacogene the callset cannot answer is a question, not a normal result
clinical_framing: research exercise; no row advises for or against giving any drug to any patient

columns.comparison_set_rate: share of matched comparison ingredients with any mapped effect
columns.genome_call: actionability words per pharmacogene; 'no call' is a result
columns.genome_flag: yes when a gene is actionable, uncallable, or outside the caller
columns.phenotype_flag: yes on either trigger; phenotype_flag_reason says which

limitations: no patient genome, so K2 can never reach its fail state (both sources flag); OnSIDES v3.1.1 ships no paediatric ADE subset (its paediatric file is a 200-label annotation gold standard), so the paediatric view comes from FAERS, which has no denominator

parameters.comparison_rule: 5 nearest approved ingredients per candidate, matched on the number of distinct adverse effects their labels carry; candidates excluded

sources.clinical: Bloom syndrome's 42 HPO terms (23 used for the flag), mapped to MedDRA in ressources/track2/transfer-it4/BLM/hpo_to_adverse_terms.tsv
sources.genomic: none: no patient genome (the pgx_summary.json read declares no gene); the genome half is not run

validation: none: no positive-control drug was fixed for the Bloom mapping (entry 156)
wording: unflagged by these two sources (not evidence of safety)
